title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
This is a perception and response failure in an autonomous driving system. The vehicle was operating in autonomous mode on residential streets when it struck a duck and did not stop. The duck was a small animal in the roadway, and the system did not detect it or did not act on it. Nothing in the reporting describes a braking event or a stop after contact.

The failure happened on public residential streets in the Mueller Lake neighbourhood, in the ordinary course of a testing operation. A human safety operator was present in the vehicle. Catching this would have required either the perception system to identify a small animal in the path, or the operator to intervene before or at the moment of contact. Avride's response was operational rather than a halt: it removed certain streets around the lake from its testing area, kept testing elsewhere, and ran simulations to check that changes would not degrade overall safety performance.

What is not established is why the duck was not detected, and whether any person or system could have prevented the collision. The claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign is a resident allegation, and Avride's investigation found no evidence for it. The reports do not establish fault, intent, or the internal cause of the vehicle's behaviour.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
A self-driving car operated by Avride in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood, causing significant community backlash. The autonomous vehicle, which had a human safety operator present, did not stop after hitting the duck that residents knew well, as it had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant. The incident generated widespread concern about whether autonomous vehicles should operate in residential areas. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode during the incident and investigated the resident's claim that it failed to stop at a stop sign, finding no evidence to support this allegation. In response to the controversy, Avride has adjusted its testing area by excluding certain streets around the lake and is evaluating technology improvements to avoid similar situations. The company continues testing but has not halted operations entirely, and it is conducting simulations to ensure any changes do not compromise overall safety performance.
